warmup.text: Answer the question on the card first. Then read a poem by Robert Louis Stevenson out loud, twice. Listen for the gallop. Today you name every part of the poem at work: form, rhyme, beat, line breaks, and comparisons.

words.text: Today you find the endings o u s, i v e and i t y in new words, and you spot the spelling shifts inside a word family. Then write your paragraph with sentences that start in different ways. Eight more notches up the coyote hole.

reading.text: Read Chapter 14, The Prospectors. The partners get ready to leave Hangtown. Watch Stubb the burro, listen to how each person talks, and notice what Praiseworthy reveals about his plan.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 14. Then rewrite your paragraph, starting with the dialogue. Make each person sound like themselves. Use the frames if you get stuck.

cards.title: A note before you read: words from 1963
cards.intro: One word near the end of Chapter 14 needs a note.

items.meaning: As the partners head into the mountains, Jack keeps an eye out for rabbits, squirrels, savages and outlaws. Savages was an insult for Native people. Putting them in a list with animals treats them as wild and dangerous.

The hills the partners walk into were the homelands of the Nisenan, Miwok and Maidu peoples, who had lived there for thousands of years. The danger ran the other way: miners took their land and rivers, and many Native people were killed or driven out.
California's Native nations are still here today, and many keep their languages and traditions alive.

cards.note: Sources: Oakland Museum of California; PBS American Experience.

virtue.name: integrity

options.t: Praiseworthy says he will come back to fight the Mountain Ox: “I gave my word, didn't I?”
Buffalo John says they'll be looking for him back next month, and Praiseworthy answers, “I'll be here.”
Praiseworthy tells Jack the truth about the boxing book, even though it means saying he did not destroy it.

virtue.line: Tap the moment that shows the most integrity. Then tell why in one sentence.
